item.title: India’s Diaspora Deposit Flows Surpass $100 Billion, FE Reports
item.description: Inflows under the Reserve Bank of India’s special overseas deposit facility have topped the $100 billion mark, the Financial Express newspaper reported Wednesday, citing officials it did not identify.

item.title: Minimax Emerges as Mainland China Investors’ New Favorite Stock
item.description: Minimax Group Inc. became the most popular Hong Kong-listed stock among mainland Chinese investors last month, in the latest sign of the latter’s voracious appetite for the country’s new-generation AI model developers.

item.title: Copper’s Rally Stalls as Worries About Global Economy Resurface
item.description: Copper fell for a second day, dropping with other metals, as resurgent oil prices fanned concerns about prospects for the world economy.

item.title: Nvidia Partner Gets Strong Demand for Rare GPU-Tied Loan in Asia
item.description: GMI Cloud, an Nvidia Corp. partner, secured commitments for more than double the amount it was seeking in a loan backed by the sale of computing power from advanced chips, underscoring strong demand for one of the first such deals in Asia.

item.title: Rupee Rally Gets a Boost From Bullish Charts and RBI’s Reserve Ammo
item.description: However, a continued increase in oil prices may dent optimism around the currency.

item.title: Unitree Plunges 50% From Peak in Fast Reversal After Huge Debut Pop
item.description: Unitree Robotics shares have tumbled 50% from their intraday peak, marking one of the steepest declines for a newcomer on Shanghai’s Star Board.

item.title: RBNZ Delivers Back-to-Back Rate Hikes to Curb Inflation
item.description: New Zealand’s central bank raised its key interest rate for a second straight meeting, aiming to shift to less stimulatory settings in an effort to head off inflationary pressures.

item.title: BOJ Board Hawk Calls for Nimble Hikes to Prevent Price Risks
item.description: Bank of Japan Board Member Hajime Takata, one of the bank’s most hawkish members, reiterated his call for nimble interest rate hikes to prevent upward price deviations, adding to growing speculation over a near-term policy move.

item.title: Australian Economy Beats Estimates, Adding to Rate-Hike Case
item.description: Australia’s economic growth unexpectedly accelerated last quarter, adding to the case for the Reserve Bank to raise interest rates again as inflation remains stubbornly strong.

item.title: Insolvent Bathla Faces 24-Hour Deadline for Deal With Creditors
item.description: Insolvent Australian property developer Bathla Group faces a 24-hour timeframe for talks with its creditors to secure short-term funding, according to a person familiar with the matter, in its last-ditch effort to avert collapse.

item.title: China Bond Sales Set to Accelerate, Putting Focus on PBOC
item.description: China’s government bond sales are expected to pick up after a lull as authorities seek to boost a sluggish economy, with increased issuance likely to prompt the central bank to inject more liquidity.

item.title: AI Startup Cognition Set to Raise Around $1 Billion at a $47 Billion Value
item.description: Artificial intelligence coding startup Cognition AI Inc. is set to close a new round of funding that would vault its valuation to about $47 billion, according to people familiar with the efforts.

item.title: Nvidia Nears $14 Billion Hugging Face Deal This Week
item.description: Nvidia Corp. is in advanced talks to acquire artificial intelligence startup Hugging Face in a transaction that may total about $14 billion, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: BOJ’s Ueda Hints at September Rate Hike as Bets on Move Mount
item.description: Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda hinted that a rate hike is likely when the board convenes for a meeting later this month, saying that officials will decide on policy with upside price risks in mind.

item.title: Gold Extends Decline as Inflation Risks Lift Fed Rate-Hike Bets
item.description: Gold extended a three-day decline as escalating attacks in the Middle East and concerns about inflation ratcheted up bets on interest rate hikes and pushed bond yields higher.

item.title: Bessent Says China Prevented G20 Communique Over Imbalance Spat
item.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said China prevented the Group of 20 from issuing a joint communique after a gathering of finance and central bank chiefs this week, due to a dispute over its giant trade surplus.

item.title: Seraphim Launches New ETF to Target Pure-Play Space Investors
item.description: Investors are being offered a new way to bet on space via a fund that focuses exclusively on a sector thrust into the limelight by the IPO of Elon Musk’s SpaceX.

item.title: S. Korea’s Inflation Picks Up on One-Off Phone Bill Effect
item.description: South Korea’s inflation topped 3% for the third time this year while an acceleration in core price gains to the fastest pace in more than three years bolstered the central bank’s case for maintaining its tightening bias.

item.title: Ambani’s Streaming Site Eyes Millions of Indian Diaspora
item.description: India’s largest video streaming platform JioHotstar is expanding overseas for the first time, launching in the UK, Canada and Singapore as it seeks to tap millions of potential viewers in the growing South Asian diaspora.

item.title: Asian Stocks Set for Declines as Oil Extends Gains: Markets Wrap
item.description: Asian stocks were set to decline Wednesday as surging oil prices pushed bond yields higher and stoked fears that resurgent inflation will force central banks to tighten monetary policy.

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Sept. 2
item.description: Oil advanced for a third session on heightened concerns about prolonged disruptions to energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz after an escalation of hostilities between the US and Iran.

item.title: Germany Plans Measures to Curb China Trade in Coming Weeks
item.description: Germany plans to agree on a package of measures in the coming weeks to counter what it sees as unfair Chinese trade practices, Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil said after visiting a BMW plant in Spartanburg, South Carolina.

item.title: Bessent’s Bond Gains Wiped Out as Treasury Yields Jump Again
item.description: The yields on the longest-dated US government bonds shot back to levels seen just before Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent shocked markets last month by expanding a buyback program in an effort to halt the rise.

item.title: Vanguard, BlackRock ETF Shuffle Lets Foreign Investors Duck US Tax
item.description: Major institutions are flipping between near-identical equity funds to avoid receiving dividends — and the 30% tax that comes with them.

item.title: Dropbox User Accounts Breached by Hackers Who Accessed Data
item.description: Hackers broke into thousands of Dropbox Inc. accounts last month, viewing and downloading material users kept on the cloud-storage platform, according to a company statement and records seen by Bloomberg News.

item.title: Apple Sets Pay Targets at $58 Million for Ternus, $47 Million for Cook
item.description: Apple Inc. said that new Chief Executive Officer John Ternus will get a compensation package worth about $58 million in fiscal 2027, while Tim Cook’s role as executive chairman will pay around $47 million.

item.title: Nokia to Rejoin Euro Stoxx 50 Index as Volkswagen Loses Its Spot
item.description: Nokia Oyj is regaining its spot in the euro area’s main stock benchmark as Volkswagen AG loses its place in the latest sign of the difficulties facing the region’s automotive industry.

item.title: Canadian Stocks Erase a Month of Gain as Tech, Banks, Gold Slide
item.description: Canadian stocks suffered their worst rout in nearly a month as an escalation in tensions in the Middle East added to worries about inflation and sparked a selloff in shares of high-flying technology and financial companies.

item.title: Canada Can Ride Out Global Bond Rout, Finance Minister Says
item.description: Finance Minister Francois-Philippe Champagne said positive investor sentiment is helping keep Canada’s borrowing costs in check despite a global bond rout, arguing the country’s finances are strong enough to handle the volatility.

item.title: Palo Alto Networks Tops Profit Outlook on AI Security Demand
item.description: The cybersecurity firm Palo Alto Networks Inc. issued a profit outlook for the year that exceeded Wall Street’s expectations, fueled by corporate demand for stronger defenses against advancing artificial intelligence systems.
